_hhs_region_9: Arizona, California, Hawaii, Nevada, and Pacific territories

Pima.notes: Home of University of Arizona — high young adult density increases transmission velocity

Maricopa.notes: Largest county in AZ by population — Phoenix metro, multiple major hospital networks

Cochise.notes: Rural county, US-Mexico border — limited healthcare access, cross-border travel exposure

Yavapai.notes: Older median age population — higher vulnerability to respiratory illness

Coconino.notes: Grand Canyon tourism creates variable travel exposure from international visitors

Pinal.notes: Fast-growing corridor between Phoenix and Tucson metro areas

Navajo.notes: Significant tribal communities — historically limited healthcare infrastructure

Apache.notes: Remote rural county — very limited healthcare access

Santa Cruz.notes: Smallest AZ county by area — highest border crossing density in the state. Nogales port of entry processes 4M+ crossings annually. Limited hospital capacity; nearest trauma center is in Tucson (65 miles). High cross-border disease transmission risk.

Yuma.notes: Agricultural and border hub — San Luis port of entry is one of the busiest commercial crossings in the US. Large seasonal migrant farmworker population with limited healthcare access. Sparse clinic coverage outside the city of Yuma.

Graham.notes: Rural mining and ranching county — nearest hospital is 45+ miles for most residents. Limited primary care providers. High occupational exposure risk in mining and agricultural communities.

La Paz.notes: Remote western AZ county — sparsely populated, large geographic area. Limited healthcare infrastructure; residents often travel to Yuma or Phoenix for specialty care.
